pages.title: Right now
text: What the March is doing as you read this. It changes with or without you.

pages.title: March weather
text: Four of the March's countries have weather of their own, beyond rain. **Ashfall** in the Ember Wastes, a **Glimmer Storm** over the Crystal Fields, a **Whiteout** on the Snow Fields and **Fen Mist** in the Reed Fen. Each closes the world in: you see less, and spirits rise by day under it as they would at night.

Each also favours one voice and hampers another. Ashfall feeds Ember Horns and chokes Wind Harps; a Glimmer Storm feeds Wake Bells and dulls Drumhearts; a Whiteout drives Wind Harps and freezes Wave Drums; Fen Mist swells Wave Drums and damps Ember Horns. Half again as much from the favoured voice, half as much from the hampered one, by default.
Weather comes and goes on its own, a chance every hour, and lasts a quarter of an hour or so. The Codex page above tells you what is running; so does the sky.

pages.title: Ley surges
text: Now and then one voice's ley threads run **bright**: a surge. Through the [Ley Lens](ley_lens) they blaze, and the lens names the voice. While it lasts, every Ley Collector whose threads carry that voice yields **double**.

The other side of it: every ley cell has a **crossing**, the point its threads meet, and standing on a bare one during a surge, with no collector near to drink it, gives you **Ley Sickness**: the ground sways and your Pulse drains. Step off, or set a collector on it and make the surge yours.
Surges run a quarter of an hour and come every hour and a half or so by default.

pages.title: Festivals
text: Every tribe keeps a **festival day**, the nine of them taking turns through a cycle of twenty-seven days. On their day the camp's fires burn, the hearth throws its colour into the air, and the Kin keep to the hearth instead of wandering.

The Elder has festival words, and if you ask to join the feast they press two of the tribe's dish into your hands with a heap of standing, once per festival. A rite performed in the camp that day earns festival thanks on top of the rite's, and eating a feast beside the hearth counts you at their table.
The Codex page above names whose day it is, and the March tells you when the day turns.

pages.title: Wandering spirits
text: Rarely, out in the March, a warm light drifts near you: a **wandering spirit**. It does not flee. Reach it and it tells you a line of its country's story and leaves a small gift, the reagent its guardian answers to, or now and then a Resonant Core, and goes.
Left alone it fades in a couple of minutes. Each country has three things to say; hear them all and you know the March a little better.
